key: Three fertilize the worlds with genial moisture: three noble Creatures cast a light before them. Three that give warmth to all attend the morning. All these have they discovered, these Vasisthas.
s: In a hymn on the Vasisthas and their birth, the verse credits them with a threefold lore; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 7.33.7, citing the Śāṭyāyanaka, reads the triads as Agni, Vāyu and the Sun in earth, air and sky, and the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas.

evidence.gloss: In the worlds, earth, mid-air and sky, the three, Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya, in order, make seed, the water that sustains all. Of these three, the three noble peoples are those led by light, headed by Āditya. And the three, Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya, shining, attend the dawn. All these, hard to know, the Vasiṣṭhas understand. Because they know the secret of these, this too is a praise of the Vasiṣṭhas. So the Śāṭyāyanaka: Agni makes seed on earth, Vāyu in mid-air, Āditya in the sky; the three peoples are the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, and their light is yonder sun; Agni, Vāyu and Āditya attend the dawn.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, 7.33.7 at [548,7]). Sāyaṇa on 7.33.7 reads the three who make seed in the worlds as Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya in earth, mid-air and sky in order, and the same three as the warm ones attending the dawn, then quotes the Śāṭyāyanaka naming the three noble peoples as the Vasus, the Rudras and the Ādityas; Wilson’s note (‘Sayana quotes Satyayana for the explanation of this verse’) confirms. The sentence says just this, attributing the Vasus/Rudras/Ādityas part as citing the Śāṭyāyanaka. Plain sense faithful: 7.33 is on the Vasisthas, their help to Sudas against the Ten Kings and Vasistha’s birth (7.33.10 to 13); ‘a threefold lore’ is a fair context gloss of the three triads they know.
